newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee ends mostly lower in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee ends mostly lower in thin trade.

text.p: London's robusta coffee futures were mostly easier in thin dealings marked by origin selling on Monday but activity was narrow, traders said.
"Most of the action is in New York where specs have been selling," said one trader.
January robusta ended $1 up on the day at $1,337 after trading in a narrow $1,342-1,320 range, while other forward contracts lost up to $17.

The January contract managed to avoid a resumption of last week's dramatic series of declines through key support levels and hovered in a tight range as funds continued to sell and trade and roasters bought on the dips.
Unlike in New York, funds were relatively quiet in London, traders said.
Values slumped to 31-month lows on Friday as the benchmark January contract slipped through key support at $1,360 and $1,340.
Technical analysts are now pegging support at $1,325, a reaction high from September 1993 on a second-month continuation basis.
They say January may struggle to regain ground lost during last week's slide as heavy resistance is indicated around $1,400. A nearer upside target is $1,360.
Physical news was scarce and players awaited new estimates of the Brazilian crop in 1997/98.

Brokers Merrill Lynch said even a small drop in Brazil's output could keep the market in a precarious state as production was likely to fall short of consumption in the current 1996/97 season by 2-3 million bags.
"This should keep the market from falling precipitously even when new crop arrivals start to appear and ease the nearby situation," Merrill Lynch said in thier latest biweekly report.
